params.body:
The other half of control#66. A gateway keeps the configuration it was given until an operator carries a new one over, on purpose: a client does not rewrite the policy of a Tier 3 gateway. The invisibility was the problem. `vera` sat in the configuration on this box for an hour while the VM served the grant from before it, and the only sign was a hand refused with `resource not in grant`: correct, and unreadable.

`elixir:control-service` now compares, per hand, the digest of the kinds and resources it writes with the digest the service publishes, and puts the difference in the job note together with what to do about it:

> the gateway serves an older grant (#agent-elixir: resources); until it is carried over, a hand is refused with "not in grant". Carry it over: scp the config.json of this box, then rehearse.sh config and a restart.

The same list in another order is not a difference (both sides sort), an agent the gateway does not know is named as such, and a gateway that publishes no digests (control before this) raises nothing.

Merge after control#66 is tagged and on the VM; before that it simply stays quiet. 661 tests, PHPStan, Pint.
params.title: De job zegt het als de VM een oudere vergunning bedient
